US Attacks Two Iranian Government Tankers

According to a report by Axios on Tuesday, the U.S. military carried out strikes against two Iranian government tankers parked on the Iranian coast north of the U.S. naval blockade line, citing an unnamed U.S. official. Another official told Axios that Trump had approved the “tanker for tanker” policy as a means to deter Iran from striking ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the report said.

Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Slams Attacks
Following the strikes, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson
Esmaeil Baqaei

slammed the U.S., saying that the strikes in the city of Kuhestak on a home that was celebrating a wedding resulted in the deaths/injuries of more than 50 people, including women and children, calling it the U.S.’s “catalogue of atrocities against the nation of Iran.”

According to a report by the New York Times on Tuesday, citing comments by local officials, as well as the Iranian Red Crescent Society, at least four people were killed in the strike on the wedding ceremony in Kuhestak, including one child and 53 people were injured.
Baqaei then pointed to earlier strikes by the U.S., including a strike on a

, which resulted in the deaths of more than 150 civilians, a majority of whom were schoolgirls. “More dangerous than the bomb itself is the normalization of bombing; and more dangerous than silence is the conversion of silence into legitimacy,” Baqaei said.

The spokesperson then said that Tehran will have a firm response to the attacks. “Those governments and international institutions that remain silent in the face of such barbarism, or seek to justify such acts, must understand that their silence is not neutrality,” he said.
Baqaei accused countries of normalizing and whitewashing “unlawful” attacks. “Turning a blind eye to injustice does not contain it; it only emboldens the perpetrators,” he said.
The United States’ catalogue of atrocities against the nation of Iran is now complete: a residential home in Kuhestak,
, was brutally attacked tonight while families were celebrating a wedding. More than 50 innocent men, women and children were martyred or wounded.
